L2t: The largest triangle inscribed in a semicircle has its base along the diameter, so its area depends only on the radius.
L3t: The maximal triangle uses the full diameter 2r as its base with its apex at the top of the arc, at height r, so the area is (1/2)(2r)(r), and negative radii must be rejected.
L4t: Return None when r is negative, otherwise return r squared, since the largest inscribed triangle has base 2r and height r.
L2f: A triangle inscribed in a semicircle must have all three vertices on the curved arc, so the diameter is never used as a side.
L3f: The largest triangle in the semicircle is the equilateral triangle with its vertices on the arc, so its area follows the equilateral formula in terms of r.
L4f: The answer is the equilateral-triangle area (sqrt(3)/4)*r^2 scaled by the radius, not r squared.
cand_true: return r*r, or None if r is negative
cand_wrong2: half of the semicircle's area, pi*r*r/4
